newsitem.title: GERMANY: German FinMin, Bundesbank deny EMU delay talk.
newsitem.headline: German FinMin, Bundesbank deny EMU delay talk.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry and Bundesbank on Friday firmly denied a market rumour that Germany was about to make a statement saying the the start of European monetary union would be delayed.
"That's ridiculous," a spokeswoman for the finance ministry in Bonn said.

A Bundesbank spokesman echoed these sentiments, noting talk that the Bundesbank itself was about to make a statement of this type was completely nonsensical as such a decision could only be taken by the finance ministry, not the central bank.
"Speculation that the Bundebank plans to make a statement on a delay in EMU is complete nonsense," he said, adding, "We are not aware of any intentions which go in this direction."

Talk that the launch of the single currency, scheduled for 1999, could be delayed apparently originated in markets in London. But it spread like wildfire with traders seeing a delay as a possibility, while conceding that such a major announcement probably would not be made out of the blue.

Problems faced by almost all European states in reining in their budget deficits to bring them under the threshold laid down in the Mastricht Treaty have led many economists to increase the probability rating of a delay in the start.
Countries which want to enter EMU in 1999 must meet set targets on inflation, exchange rates, interest rates, deficits and public debt.
